content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper proposes robust referring video object segmentation (R2-VOS) by adding negative sentences for R-VOS. The authors use textual embedding to build relational cycle consistency to enhance the visual language project process. They achieve the state-of-the-art results on both R-VOS and R2-VOS benchmarks.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength:
1. Biggest contribution: Addressed the false-alarm problem of R-VOS task, which is indeed exists and important. Previous R-VOS methods cannot handle unpaired video-text inputs (they tend to output false positive masks).

2. On the basis of 1, propose a cycle consistency model to handle the R2-VOS task, by introducing a text reconstruction module to discriminate whether the language expression is positve or negative.

3. Their model achieves SOTA scores in both traditional R-VOS and proposed R2-VOS tasks

4. Detailed ablations about the features of the proposed model.

Weakness:

1. The proposed setting itself. A picture can have many descriptions, including the negative sentences. However, this paper does not well explore the effect of different negative sentences when make such settings. The main contribution of this paper is adding Relational Cycle Consistency loss via existing dynamic convolution on an existing framework (ReferFormer-CVPR-2022) This makes this submission weak. In particular, the proposed method achieves nearly full-performance (95%). This makes the proposed setting unnecessary and hard to follow. Maybe a better discussion on the new metric design can be carried.  Moreover, the motivation of the proposed setting is not clear. 

2. Many related works are missing. I can not find any related works for image grounding, image referring segmentation or robustness analysis of segmentation or detection. 

3. Shuffling the expressions and videos in the evaluation set is a simple way to construct robustness evaluation sets. But unmatched text-video pairs do not necessarily mean 'un-exist'. A 'negative' expression may happen to depict some objects in the new video. So that the negative pair has actually become a 'positive' one. The paper ignores the potential question with their proposed R2-VOS.

4. Lack of the visualization or analysis of the output of text reconstruction module. 

5. What does Relational Cycle Consistency help for your Robust R-VOS?

6. Why use the dynamic kernel technique in the early grounding?  Moreover, the motivation of such design is also unclear.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: Clarity, Quality are easy to follow. The Novelty of the setting is Good, while the solutions are not.
content.summary_of_the_review: I concern about what are the real contribution of this paper. Also, I can not understand the motivation of such setting or network design.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This submission proposes a framework for addressing the Referring VOS task with semantic consensus and the extended new task (Robust Referring VOS) without semantic consensus. To promote this new task, the authors construct a benchmark dataset named R2-Youtube-VOS. Also, the authors leverage the cycle consistency to consolidate and discriminate the semantic consensus. Then, they propose an early grounding module to optimize the primary and dual problems parallel. Experiments on three benchmarks (Ref-DAVIS17, Ref-Youtube-VOS, and R2-Youtube-VOS) show that the proposed model could achieve the SOTA performance.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
This submission has a good starting point to explore the semantic consensus problem in the referring VOS field. Also, it is well-organized and -presented. However, some concerns still need to be addressed in the rebuttal period.

- Why introduce the cycle at text-video-text but not video-text-video? Could the authors provide more validation for this assumption? Does language modality dominate more than visual modality for this task?
- As in Lines-128, several video-related works focus on the cycle-consistence, such as [1*,2*]. Of note, the early idea for cycle-consistence that we can trace back to is CycleGAN [3*]. These works could offer more inspiration for the authors.
- Does the textual encoder trainable?
- Why use the dynamic kernel technique in the early grounding?
- Have the authors taken further fine-tuning for ReferFormer and the proposed model on the R2-Youtube-VOS benchmark? Table 4 also indicates that the proposed model uses a negative training strategy, but other competitors in Table.1 do not adopt this strategy. The comparison in Table 1 maybe not be fair. This also raises the reviewer's next concern.
- This may exist as a fortunate case here: the linguistic caption for pair-A may also match or partly match the visual image from pair-B.   Have the authors checked all the constructed positive and negative pairs for the R2-Youtube-VOS benchmark?
- Lack of comparison with the latest R-VOS models [4*,5*,6*,7*]. The authors may over-claim the SOTA performance in Lines-77.
- Could the authors measure the J & F performance on the R2-Youtube-VOS benchmark?
- How to balance the different factor lambda for a bunch of loss functions?


[1*] Learning Correspondence from the Cycle-consistency of Time. CVPR, 2019.
[2*] Temporal Cycle-Consistency Learning. CVPR, 2019.
[3*] Unpaired Image-to-Image Translation using Cycle-Consistent Adversarial Networks. ICCV, 2017.
[4*] Multi-Attention Network for Compressed Video Referring Object Segmentation. ACM MM 2022
[5*] Locater: Local-Global Context Aware Transformer for Language-Guided Video Segmentation. 2022
[6*] Modeling Motion with Multi-Modal Features for Text-Based Video Segmentation. CVPR, 2022.
[7*] Multi-Level Representation Learning with Semantic Alignment for Referring Video Object Segmentation

Other minor issues:
- Conferences or journals have formally accepted several works; for example, ReferFormer (Wu et al., 2022) and MTTR (Botach et al., 2021) have been accepted by CVPR 2022, video-swing-transformer has been accepted by CVPR 2022. Please check all arXiv items and update them in the reference section.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
(a) The clarity and quality are good.
(b) The novelty is satisfactory to address a new problem (semantic consensus) in R-VOS but lacks some critical evaluations and support. 
(d) The authors provide enough details for reproducibility.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper introduces the Robust R-VOS task that accepts unpaired video and text as inputs. In addition, a pipeline is proposed to optimize the primary referring and dual expression reconstruction task. A relational cycle consistency constraint is proposed to enhance the semantic alignment between different modalities. The proposed approach achieves state-of-the-art results on three datasets.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strengths:
1) This paper proposed the Robust R-Youtube-VOS dataset that is used to measure the robustness of R-VOS models.
2) The relational cycle consistency is applied to preserve the structure of the feature space rather than point-wise consistency. The proposed cycle consistency achieves better results than point-wise consistency.
3)The proposed approach achieves state-of-the-art on three datasets, and some ablation studies are conducted to validate the effectiveness of each component.
4)The paper is generally well written. 

Weakness:
1) My main concern is about novelty. In this paper, for negative videos set M_o is empty. For some R-VOS methods, they are able to align the semantic information of different modalities, and they also overcome the problem that unpaired video and text as inputs so that Robust R-VOS does not need to be studied separately.

2) This paper proposed a new task and proposed a new dataset. However, the paper makes the ablation study based on the traditional Ref-DAVIS17, and Ref-Youtube-VOS.

3) This paper leverages text reconstruction to reconstruct the text feature to measure semantic consensus. It is commonly used for Video-Language tasks.

4) In formula 8,  how to measure semantic consensus between Reconstructed text feature and text feature is not explained.

5) It is not clear how to evaluate this model on the Robust R-VOS dataset. Is the model trained on the Ref-Youtube-VOS dataset and directly evaluated on the Robust R-VOS dataset?

6) The ablation experiments in this paper are performed on the Ref-Youtube-VOS dataset, which does not need to consider this problem that unpaired video and text as inputs, so different modules need be used separately to verify their effectiveness.

7) Can you more clearly introduce the source of the negative sample videos in the dataset? If these videos are also from the Ref-Youtube-VOS dataset, each video in the entire dataset will correspond to a positive text message. In order to better verify the robustness of the model, videos that do not correspond to text information in the entire dataset should be added.

content.summary_of_the_review: Overall, the writing quality of the whole manuscript is not good. Also, the experimental results especially the ablation study is weak.

content.summary_of_the_paper: The paper introduces a new task, named Robust R-VOS motivated by the strict assumption of R-VOS: the object must exist in the video given any descriptive text. In addition, to deal with this extended task from R-VOS, the paper leverages the cycle consistency in the text-video-text transformation and discriminates the semantic consensus. In experiments, the paper extends the Ref-Youtube-VOS validation set with extra negative videos and proposes a new metric to verify their performance. The method achieves SOTA performance on several R-VOS benchmarks (Ref-DAVIS17 and Ref-Youtube-VOS) and tackles the Robust R-VOS task as well.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength:
- The proposed task, R$^2$-VOS, is intuitive and reasonable. Since the assumption about the positive correspondence is too strict, the R-VOS method should consider first whether it is a match.
- The proposed model not only well solves the proposed R$^2$-VOS task but also boosts the performance on the original R-VOS task.
- The loss of relational consistency is insightful and provides a new perspective to constrain the reconstruction. Also, the authors sufficiently prove its effectiveness in Table 3.

Weakness:
- Except for the V-T project, is there any significant innovation compared to ReferFormer[1]? It seems the technical contribution is weak and incremental in terms of the architecture.
- The novel metric proposed in the paper seems too trivial that the method reaches ~95 already. It would be better to design a more challenging metric if the authors want to make the tasks more solid.
- It is not fair to directly evaluate the previous model on the R$^2$-VOS tasks since there is no binary flag to detect whether it is the wrong text-video pair. Maybe the authors can adopt a simple way to flag some obvious misalignment between text and video and discard the prediction in total. For example, compute the confidence of the mask prediction by the compactness of the mask. In that way, the results are more convincing. 
- Miss the experiments on large transformer backbone, (e.g., Video-Swin-B). The usage of the large backbone is supposed to boost performance. It would be better if the results are provided.

[1] Language As Queries for Referring Video Object Segmentation. CVPR 2022.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The paper proposes a novel task formulation, R$^2$-VOS, and resolves it well by cycle consistency. The paper writing is clear and easy to follow. Implementation details are concise and reproducible.
content.summary_of_the_review: Overall, it is a paper with the good motivation that the robust referring video object task is novel and insightful for the community. But the implementation contains flaws, like the metric and architecture. I am glad to hear the responses from the authors.

content.title: $\mathrm{R}^2$-VOS: Robust Referring Video Object Segmentation via Relational Cycle Consistency
content.abstract: Referring video object segmentation (R-VOS) aims to segment the object masks in a video given a referring linguistic expression to the object. R-VOS introduces human language in the traditional VOS loop to extend flexibility, while all current studies are based on a strict assumption: the object depicted by the expression must exist in the video, namely, the expression and video must have an object-level semantic consensus. This is often violated in real-world applications where an expression can be queried to false videos, and existing methods always fail due to abusing the assumption. In this work, we emphasize that studying semantic consensus is necessary to improve the robustness of R-VOS. Accordingly, we pose an extended task from R-VOS without the semantic consensus assumption, named Robust R-VOS ($\mathrm{R}^2$-VOS). The new task essentially corresponds to the joint modeling of the primary R-VOS problem and its dual (text reconstruction). We embrace the observation that the textual embedding spaces have relational structure consistency in the text-video-text transformation cycle that links the primary and dual problems. We leverage the cycle consistency to consolidate and discriminate the semantic consensus, thus advancing the primary task. We then propose an early grounding module to enable the parallel optimization of the primary and dual problems. To measure the robustness of R-VOS models against unpaired videos and expressions, we construct a new evaluation dataset, $\mathrm{R}^2$-Youtube-VOS. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our method not only identifies negative text-video pairs but also improves the segmentation accuracy for positive pairs with superior disambiguating ability. Our model achieves the state-of-the-art performance on Ref-DAVIS17, Ref-Youtube-VOS, and $\mathrm{R}^2$-Youtube-VOS dataset.
